short: What a business owns and owes on one specific date.
seoTitle: Balance Sheet — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: A balance sheet is a snapshot on one date of what a business owns, what it owes and what belongs to the owners. Part of the free Setu business glossary.
definition: A balance sheet is a snapshot on one date of what a business owns, what it owes and what belongs to the owners. Assets always equal liabilities plus equity, which is where the name comes from.
bodyHtml:
Why Balance Sheet matters

The P&L shows performance over a period; the balance sheet shows condition at a moment. Lenders read it first, because it reveals debt, working capital and how much of the business is genuinely owned.

Balance Sheet formula

Assets = Liabilities + Equity

Any imbalance means the underlying entries are incomplete.

How Balance Sheet works in practice

Read it as a whole. Rising stock and receivables alongside a shrinking bank balance tells the story of a profitable business quietly running out of cash.

faq.question: What is the difference between a balance sheet and a P&L?
faq.answer: The balance sheet is a position on a date; the P&L covers a period of trading.

faq.question: Why does profit not appear on the balance sheet directly?
faq.answer: It does, inside retained earnings, which accumulates profits left in the business.
